newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates lower after heavy lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates lower after heavy lending.

text.p: Interbank rates were lower across the board on Monday after heavy lending of one-month money over the past week, dealers said.
The softness also reflected a drop in the overnight rate to as low as 6.0 percent on Friday after aggressive lending by foreign banks, they said.
"There has been a heavy lending of one-month money. I'm not sure if it was Bank Negara's intervention or the big banks themselves were lending," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said with maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 1.5 billion ringgit this week expected to improve liquidity further, interbank rates were likely to fall back to their earlier levels soon.
Rates had stayed firm over the past one month after massive intervention by Bank Negara in the foreign exchange market caused a liquidity squeeze.
One-, two- and three-week money were at 7.50/80 percent against 8.00/20 percent on Friday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 7.80/90 percent from 8.20/30, and three-month was also at 7.80/90 percent against 8.00/10.
The overnight rate was expected to trade around 7.0 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher, but trading volume was thin.
At 0240 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up four points to 92.10, or an implied yield of 7.90 percent.
The September contract rose six to 92.51, or 7.49 percent, and December was also up six to 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
